title: Foundation activation ledger bridge
description: Objective: adapt the shared durable EffectActivationCommitted authority from task-df29871bfc2441659efb3f763ddb23db to the Foundation Claude dispatch without duplicating its codec or transaction. Deliverable: daemon production ports that consume df298's strict activation reader/commit adapter for the Foundation request, perform durable UNUSED-to-consumed grant CAS plus preflight/observed launch-registration updates as append-only exact-version events, and expose the current effect/session binding derived from the committed ACTIVE intent and active lease ownerSessionRef. Consumers: task-6cbff01023b14b26a78fc5e3eb1dd8a9 and the coordination adapter. NOT in scope: physical launch, HTTP registry, graph admission, result manifests, schema/DDL, or reimplementing claim/activation reducers. Hard dependency: df298 DONE and task-c81953d210f14cdeb9f6070a443b6750 public launcher overlay.
definitionOfDone: The bridge imports df298's production activation record/strict reader and never defines a competing EffectActivationCommitted codec, aggregate identity, or initial commit.

Grant consumption and pending/observed process registration are durable exact-version transitions bound to activation digest, grantId, wrapper, attempt, lock and process identity; replay returns the byte-identical stored transition and conflicts refuse with exact code/layer before provider open.

A frozen typed effect/session reader returns BOUND only when the durable activation is coherent ACTIVE/RUNNING, the lease is ACTIVE and unexpired, query effectId equals intentId, and sessionId equals lease.ownerSessionRef; absent/stale/terminal/cross-project/malformed/unreadable evidence is ABSENT or UNKNOWN with exact stable code/layer.

Real SqliteEventStore concurrency/injected-throw tests assert positive race counts, one winning CAS/registration chain, raw public event/decision counts, and no partial durable authority; no ad-hoc SQLite objects or DatabaseSync access.

The coordination adapter production port maps only BOUND to the exact frozen positive binding and preserves the existing COORDINATION_TERMINAL_BINDING_INVALID/ADDRESS refusal for every negative/unknown case; task-6cbff010 consumes the same ports.
taskRails: Hard-depend on task-df29871 and task-c81953d2; block rather than copying their authority.
Use existing @moe/store event/decision/expected-version transactions only; no schema or DDL.
TDD exact codes/layers and nonzero generated cases; public roots across packages; target <=250 lines and split before 400.
Derive session identity only from the committed lease ownerSessionRef and effect identity only from committed intentId; caller values may only be equality checks.

implementationPlan.description: Create the focused transition contract/codec without restating `EffectActivationCommitted`, its initial codec, aggregate derivation, or initial commit. Define record version `moe-foundation-activation-transition/1`, the exact ordered tags/events `GRANT_CONSUMED`/`FoundationActivationGrantConsumed`, `PREFLIGHT_REGISTERED`/`FoundationLaunchPreflightRegistered`, and `PROCESS_OBSERVED`/`FoundationLaunchProcessObserved`, and fixed tag-specific primitive tuples sealed by SHA-256 so encode/decode is canonical and byte-comparable. RESTATES NOTHING FROM df298. The module imports only node:crypto. It declares no EffectActivationCommitted record, no ACTIVATION_LEDGER_* code, no aggregate derivation and no commit: `grep -c "ACTIVATION_LEDGER\|deriveActivationAggregateId\|EffectActivationCommitted"` over it is 0. Sequence 1 stays df298's event.

Shape: record version `moe-foundation-activation-transition/1`; ordered tags GRANT_CONSUMED / PREFLIGHT_REGISTERED / PROCESS_OBSERVED mapped to event types FoundationActivationGrantConsumed / FoundationLaunchPreflightRegistered / FoundationLaunchProcessObserved. GRANT_TUPLE = (tag, activationDigest, grantId, intentId, attemptId, wrapperIdentity); REGISTRATION_TUPLE adds (lockIdentity, processIdentity, bootstrapCredentialDigest, registeredAt). Encoding is length-first framing of PLAIN UTF-8 strings — no JSON, so there is no key order, no duplicate-key ambiguity and no number to round — sealed by a trailing SHA-256 over the body. Decode verifies the seal BEFORE parsing framing, then re-encodes the validated tuple and requires the digest to reproduce, so a stored payload is byte-comparable to a fresh encoding without trusting the framing that produced it. A GRANT_CONSUMED transition must carry null in all four registration slots, so a registration field cannot be smuggled onto the grant tag.

NO SECRET COPIED: `grep -c "leaseToken\|leaseProof\|authorityHashRef"` over the file is 0. Only the credential DIGEST crosses, which is all the launch-lock protocol itself handles.

Descriptor-safe snapshot: `snapshotFoundationRecord` uses Reflect.ownKeys (catches symbol keys Object.keys misses), requires the own-key count to match exactly, and refuses any slot that is not an ENUMERABLE own DATA descriptor — so an accessor or a proxy fails closed instead of running a getter inside a refuse-only guard. Both Reflect.ownKeys and getOwnPropertyDescriptor are wrapped, because a revoked proxy throws from either.

Bounded decoding: TextDecoder("utf-8", {fatal:true}) so mis-framed bytes refuse instead of becoming U+FFFD; MAX_TRANSITION_BYTES 65_536; MAX_TEXT_CHARS 400. Outputs are frozen.

TWO TRAPS HIT AND FIXED HERE, both worth the next agent's attention:
1. My first draft wrote the control-character guard as a regex with backslash-u escapes. The Write tool JSON-DECODED them, so real control bytes (NUL through 0x1f, 0x7f) landed in the source: `grep` reported "Binary file matches" and the class had silently become `[space-hyphen]`, which would have rejected every identifier containing a hyphen. It typechecked clean. Replaced with a code-point walk (`code < 0x20 || code === 0x7f`) using hex numeric literals — no escape sequence survives in the file. Verified with `grep -aP '[\x00-\x08\x0b-\x1f\x7f]'` returning zero hits.
2. Validation reads values through typed guards, never `String(value)`: a hostile object with a throwing toString would otherwise throw out of a guard whose job is to refuse.

Binding vocabulary at layer FOUNDATION_ACTIVATION_BINDING: ABSENT { NOT_FOUND, QUERY_MISMATCH, TERMINAL, LEASE_INACTIVE, LEASE_EXPIRED }, UNKNOWN { QUERY_INVALID, PROJECT_MISMATCH, ACTIVATION_INCOHERENT, EVIDENCE_MALFORMED, EVIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS, EVIDENCE_UNREADABLE, SCAN_INCOMPLETE }, plus frozen constructors and the BOUND result type.

implementationPlan.description: Extend the 71-line reader, without changing `readActivationLedgerRecord`, with a history fold and `readCurrentEffectSessionBinding(store, projectId, effectId, sessionId, nowMilliseconds)`. The history fold requires one aggregate with contiguous sequences, isolates sequence 1 and calls the strict df298 reader on that singleton, then admits only the exact optional prefix GRANT_CONSUMED -> PREFLIGHT_REGISTERED -> PROCESS_OBSERVED and rechecks every carried activation/grant/intent/attempt/wrapper/lock/process identity. Re-parse intent/attempt/grant through the public runner parsers, require `validateActivationCommit` COHERENT and its digest equal the stored activationDigest, parse the lease through public scheduler `parseLeaseRecord`, require the durable lease equal `effectIntent.leaseBinding`, ACTIVE intent/RUNNING attempt, ACTIVE lease, configured store health plus sequence-1 decisionTrace project, and no caller-derived positive identity. For lookup, paginate `readEventsAfter(0n, 100)` with monotonic/no-empty-progress checks, validate every initial-event candidate, and require exactly one matching committed intent; any unreadable candidate or incomplete/ambiguous scan is UNKNOWN. Return frozen exact `{status:'BOUND', effectId:<committed intentId>, sessionId:<committed lease.ownerSessionRef>, activationDigest}` only when query equality and liveness hold. Validate safe millisecond input, use `Math.floor(nowMilliseconds/1000)`, and expire only when seconds are greater than the deadline. Finish this production file <=250 lines; its existing LF bridge already re-exports it.

Implement the synchronous Foundation launcher authority on the existing activation aggregate. A factory captures store, asserted project, df298 aggregateId, base CommandDecisionKey/correlation, and synchronous clock; derive phase-specific command/event identities deterministically. `consumeGrantDurably` runs the public runner grant transition, equality-checks the caller grant/wrapper against the strict durable initial record, and commits the canonical GRANT_CONSUMED payload at expectedVersion 1. `commitProcessRegistration` snapshots the public ClaudeRegistrationCommit, parses the claim through the public runner parser, requires original prior null, validates the stored prefix plus intent/wrapper/attempt/lock relations, and commits PREFLIGHT at expectedVersion 2 or PROCESS_OBSERVED at expectedVersion 3; the persisted PREFLIGHT is never supplied back as launcher prior. Set committedResultBytes equal to event payload. On REPLAYED, decode response.decision.resultBytes, require byte equality with the persisted event at the exact sequence and all current context, and return the stored successor/registration; candidate drift refuses. Map malformed grant and wrapper errors to existing `EFFECT_GRANT_MALFORMED/KERNEL` and `GRANT_WRAPPER_MISMATCH/GRANT`, durable duplicate to `GRANT_ALREADY_CONSUMED/GRANT`, activation drift/unreadability to REFUSED or SUSPECT `ACTIVATION_COMMIT_INCOHERENT/ACTIVATION`; map registration malformed, conflict, and uncertainty to `LAUNCH_LOCK_MALFORMED`, `LAUNCH_LOCK_IDENTITY_CONFLICT`, or SUSPECT `LAUNCH_LOCK_SUSPECT`, all at `LAUNCH_LOCK`, with exact legs `GRANT_CONSUME`, `PREFLIGHT_REGISTER`, `PROCESS_OBSERVE`. No Promise/thenable, raw SQLite, DDL, or physical launch. Export the frozen authority ports and a `createFoundationClaudeLauncher` call site that passes them to bare-root `createClaudeLauncher`, so task-6cb can consume the composed launcher rather than reconstructing c819. Keep the TS source <=250 lines and add its exact LF bridge.

SHAPE. `createFoundationLauncherAuthority(options)` returns a FROZEN `ClaudeLauncherAuthority` — exactly the two ports c819 asks for, both synchronous, no Promise and no thenable. Options carry df298's aggregateId (never re-derived here), the asserted projectId, a base CommandDecisionKey, a correlationId and the store port. `FoundationLaunchStore` names only commitExpectedVersionDecision and readEvents: no DDL, no raw SQLite, no `...WithApply` variant that would hand out a DatabaseSync.

DETERMINISTIC PHASE IDENTITIES. commandId `<base>:<TAG>`, correlationId `<base>:<TAG>`, eventId `<committed grantId>:<TAG>`. The grant id is COPIED from the committed activation, so store-wide event-id uniqueness keeps working for the tail exactly as it does for sequence 1. Versions/sequences: GRANT_CONSUMED 1/2, PREFLIGHT_REGISTERED 2/3, PROCESS_OBSERVED 3/4.

GRANT PORT. Pure `consumeActivationGrant` runs FIRST as an oracle; its refusal travels with the runner's own code and layer, restamped with the leg via the published `withLeg` — EFFECT_GRANT_MALFORMED/KERNEL and GRANT_WRAPPER_MISMATCH/GRANT are asserted verbatim. Then the caller's grantId/intentId/wrapperIdentity are equality-checked against the STRICT durable initial record (a foreign but well-formed grant is REFUSED ACTIVATION_COMMIT_INCOHERENT/ACTIVATION). Only then the CAS at expectedVersion 1. Conflict -> GRANT_ALREADY_CONSUMED/GRANT. Unreadable activation or a throw -> SUSPECT ACTIVATION_COMMIT_INCOHERENT/ACTIVATION. The returned successor is built from the COMMITTED grant (state CONSUMED, version durable+1), never echoed from the caller.

REGISTRATION PORT. Descriptor-safe snapshot of the public ClaudeRegistrationCommit (exact keys phase/registration/claim/prior); an unclassifiable phase refuses LAUNCH_LOCK_MALFORMED with leg null, since no phase means no leg. Claim parsed through the published `parseEffectClaim`. A non-null prior refuses LAUNCH_LOCK_IDENTITY_CONFLICT: the persisted PREFLIGHT is a RESERVATION and is never handed back as the launcher's prior. Relations checked before any write: the durable prefix must already end with GRANT_CONSUMED (for preflight) or PREFLIGHT_REGISTERED (for observed), registration.wrapperIdentity must equal both the claim's and the committed grant's, registration.lockIdentity must equal the claim's, and claim.intentId must equal the committed intentId. Then CAS at expectedVersion 2 or 3. Malformed payload -> LAUNCH_LOCK_MALFORMED, conflict -> LAUNCH_LOCK_IDENTITY_CONFLICT, throw -> SUSPECT LAUNCH_LOCK_SUSPECT, all at LAUNCH_LOCK with legs PREFLIGHT_REGISTER / PROCESS_OBSERVE.

REPLAY IS PROVED, NOT ASSUMED. committedResultBytes === the event payload. On a REPLAYED disposition the port requires BOTH `response.decision.resultBytes` AND the persisted event at this phase's exact sequence to byte-match what this call would have written, then decodes the STORED bytes and answers from them. The store's replay identity does not cover the events array, so without that check a replay could report success for bytes nobody committed. Any drift refuses.

ONE ASSERTION OF MINE WAS WRONG AND IS NOW CORRECT. The race test asserted the store held exactly 2 PUBLIC events after one connection lost. It holds 3: a refused expected-version decision legitimately appends its own AUDIT event (NO_BUSINESS_EFFECT carries auditEventId), which lands in the global stream but NOT on the target aggregate. The aggregate assertions (exactly 2 events, version 2, exact ordered event types) were already right and passed. I replaced the raw global count with the invariant that actually matters: exactly ONE FoundationActivationGrantConsumed and exactly ONE EffectActivationCommitted exist STORE-WIDE. Weakening this to "the aggregate looks right" would have missed a second grant consumed on another aggregate; a raw global count instead measures the store's audit behaviour, not mine.

implementationPlan.note:
The unconditional stub is gone. `resolveEffectBinding` now calls `readCurrentEffectSessionBinding(store, projectId, query.effectId, query.sessionId, query.now)` on the adapter's OWN store — the same `store` the session authority, recipient registry and durable mailbox already use. No caller-injectable positive resolver was added and none exists: `CoordinationAdapterOptions` is unchanged at {clock, projectId, store}, so nothing on the constructor surface can hand this port an answer.

Mapping: only `status === "BOUND"` becomes the exact frozen plain `{bound:true, effectId, sessionId}`, and BOTH ids come from the reader's committed values (intentId off the committed intent, sessionId off the committed lease ownerSessionRef) — never echoed from the query. Every ABSENT, every UNKNOWN and every throw collapses to the single frozen NO_EFFECT_BINDING, so no internal code, layer or aggregate id can leak: a refusal cannot be used as a probe for someone else's effect. `isBoundEffect` in @moe/coordination requires bound===true plus both ids echoing the query, so the unchanged service answers COORDINATION_TERMINAL_BINDING_INVALID at ADDRESS for every non-positive.

In ONE test, with the same query object throughout: before seeding, resolveEffectBinding is non-positive, `send` to the terminal address refuses COORDINATION_TERMINAL_BINDING_INVALID/ADDRESS, `read` on that mailbox refuses with the same code (the port gates both endpoints), and lifecycleDigest over the session authority plus the committed recipient ledger is unchanged — zero authority mutation on refusal. Then ONE activation is committed through df298's own commitActivationLedgerRecord, and with nothing else changed the port answers {bound:true,...}, the identical send is ACCEPTED, and the read returns a PAGE with exactly 1 item. Same test then re-checks: a different session asking about the same effect is non-positive, an uncommitted effectId is non-positive, a now past the durable lease deadline is non-positive, and after `state.reopen()` (fresh handle, fresh adapter) the positive still holds — so the answer is durable, not in-process.

planningNotes.risks: Clock units differ: CoordinationEffectQuery.now is epoch milliseconds, scheduler LeaseRecord.serverWallDeadline is wall seconds; convert with floor(now/1000), and follow scheduler overdue semantics (`wallSeconds > deadline`), so equality is still live. Only existing runner SupervisorFailure codes/layers may cross the launcher callbacks; daemon-local reader codes would be decoded as malformed. A durable PREFLIGHT row is a reservation, never the launcher's priorRegistration; STARTED receives the original prior (normally null) and validates the stored prefix separately. Same-key replay must be distinguished from a different-key duplicate: replay reads the persisted event and decision result bytes, while a competing command refuses and never opens. The global scan is a completeness proof: malformed initial candidates, duplicate matches, thrown/page-truncated reads, non-monotonic cursors, or project drift are UNKNOWN, never ABSENT/BOUND.
